$comment: A unit of work organised around a goal. The goal is what makes it a task: without one there is activity, but no task, because nothing says where it ends. It terminates — the goal is achieved, or becomes impossible, or is released. That is what makes a task the ephemeral thing and a duty the standing one, and it is why duties are discharged OVER tasks: the duty stands while task after task is raised against it, each ending, none of them ending the duty. A task holds subtasks, or work-items, or both, and at least one of something — but subtasks are tasks, so the descent has to stop somewhere: every branch bottoms out in work-items, and those in work-units, which are atomic. A tree of subtasks that never reaches a work-unit is a plan to plan. The stopping point is practical rather than formal — decompose while the chance of failure times the cost of failure is worth the trouble, and stop when it is not.

name.$comment: What the task is called, as it is said.

goal.$comment: What counts as done, as commands a machine runs. Prose is refused: a goal that cannot fail is a goal nobody can grade, and a worker handed one will substitute a task it can finish for the task it was given. At least one, because a task whose goal nobody stated has no boundary and is not a task.

discharges.$comment: The duty this task is raised against. Names a duty and must resolve to one: a task discharging nothing is work nobody owed, which is a real thing that happens and is worth naming as what it is rather than filing as a duty.

subtasks.$comment: The tasks it breaks into. Each is a task in its own right, with its own goal — that is what lets the decomposition go down as far as the stakes warrant. A task may have these, or work-items, or both.

work-items.$comment: The work-items it holds directly — the trackable entries, the things that actually get done. A task may have these, or subtasks, or both, but somewhere down every branch there must be these, and they must reach work-units: work-items are where a task stops being a container and starts being work.

plan.$comment: The order and conditions the subtasks and work-items run under — in sequence, on a condition, at the same time, or until something holds. Not always known in advance; it may be filled in as earlier ones finish and more is known.

$comment-absences: No worker or assignee: who does it belongs to the dispatch, not to the task, and a task that named its worker could not be handed to anyone else. No status, and no achieved, failed or abandoned key: a task terminates one of those three ways and which one is a readout — run the goal. A task that could assert its own completion is marking its own homework, which is the entire thing the goal exists to prevent.
